FINDINGS:

A2-F1 | BLOCKER | Death saves ignore saving-throw aid: record_death_save decides on the unmodified natural d20, contradicting SRD p.98
- Invariant and authority:
  - SRD 5.1 p.98: "You are in the hands of fate now, aided only by spells and features that improve your chances of succeeding on a saving throw. Roll a d20. If the roll is 10 or higher, you succeed."
  - Aid examples: Bless, p.122: "the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw". Aura of Protection, p.32: "a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier". Ring of Protection, p.237: "+1 bonus to AC and saving throws".
  - ADR 0020 §3 and transition design §5.9 condition 6: a capability in force declares operation, inputs and exclusions, and fails closed. record_death_save is a bounded-procedure entry of DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_INVENTORY (deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:329-351).
  - Charter: engine behaviour contradicting the SRD letter is a defect.
- Evidence:
  - toolRecordDeathSave.ts:21-33: "Record a natural d20 death-save result". Schema: roll "Natural d20 result (1-20), unmodified.", additionalProperties false.
  - hpLifecycle.ts:763-808 resolveDeathSaveTransition decides success as roll >= 10. combatantLifecycle.ts:535-575 does the same for player-character-rules combatants.
  - Declared operation: "10 or more is a success, less than 10 a failure". No exclusion mentions save bonuses.
  - System prompt (protocol.ts:330-337): "roll a d20 each of their turns and record it with record_death_save".
  - The pack record rule:death-saving-throws (p.98) carries the "aided only by" clause verbatim. The DM is shown a rule that the only state path cannot honour.
  - Probe p01-death-save.ts:
    - {roll:8, modifier:3} -> invalid_args "args.modifier is not allowed";
    - naturals 8, 9, 9 -> failure, failure, dead.
    - Under Bless (+1d4, at least +1), naturals 9, 9, 9 are three SRD successes, so the PC is stable. The engine records the PC as dead.
- Reachability: live. It affects every dying PC, and every dying player-character-rules combatant, with an active saving-throw bonus: an ally's Bless, a Paladin 6+ Aura of Protection, Ring or Cloak of Protection, Stone of Good Luck.
- Consequence:
  - Wrong canonical life/death outcome: failures are recorded where the SRD gives successes, so a PC is killed or denied stabilization.
  - No truthful path exists:
    - the modifier input is refused;
    - passing a non-natural value violates the tool contract and still mishandles natural 1 and natural 20;
    - no other tool writes death-save counters.
- Siblings:
  - Query: grep "roll >= 10|roll === 20|roll === 1" in state/*.ts, plus every tool that takes a natural roll.
  - Affected: both record_death_save paths.
  - Correct as is: restore_usage's recharge d6 and the wand's last-charge d20 use the d20 face, as the SRD requires.
  - Unaffected: resolve_check and resolve_concentration accept declared modifiers; stabilize_character takes no roll.
  - No test or doc covers aided death saves.
- Suggested closure: record_death_save, on both paths, accepts DM-declared modifiers and advantage as resolve_check does (MODIFIERS_SCHEMA). Success is total >= 10. Natural 1 (two failures) and natural 20 (regain 1 HP) stay on the d20 face. Update the inventory operation and inputs. Evidence: one generalized invariant test over (natural, bonus) including the 1/20 edges and totals 9/10, on the character and combatant paths. Narrowing to a declared exclusion is not proportionate, because aided death saves would then be unrecordable.
- Recurrence alias: no registry row. Same class as the o9bd.16 L4 deterministic-capability-correctness findings (an in-force capability that is wrong for a reachable input).

A2-F2 | NON-BLOCKER | World-time lifecycle contract: combat rounds and the instructed time tool never advance the canonical clock; minute/hour timers cannot be declared in rounds; a truthful "expired" is refused. Effects outlive their printed duration.
- Invariant and authority:
  - SRD p.90: "A round represents about 6 seconds in the game world."
  - SRD p.102: "A spell's duration is the length of time the spell persists. A duration can be expressed in rounds, minutes, hours".
  - Bless is "Concentration, up to 1 minute" (p.122).
  - Dawn recharges, e.g. Wand of Secrets p.249: "regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn".
  - Stable recovery, p.98: "regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours".
  - ADR 0020 §3 and §5.9 conditions 6 (declared exclusions, fail closed) and 9 (explicit limits).
  - The F3 contract the DM is given: "Active effects (F3 lifecycle; end via end_effect, never prose)"; start_effect "The engine enforces the lifecycle".
- Evidence:
  - (a) activeEffects.ts:4988-4999 forces the declared duration to equal the record's amount and unit. Probe p11: Bless declared as 10 rounds is refused with "the spell record's duration is 1 minute(s); the declared duration must match it".
  - (b) Combat rounds never move clock.elapsed_minutes. Probe p10: Bless is still active after 13 rounds with the clock at 0. close_combat_instance expires only round timers anchored to the instance. Probe p12d: Bless is still active after close, and later damage requests a concentration save for it.
  - (c) end_effect with "expired" is refused at activeEffects.ts:6141-6146 after 11 full rounds: "runs until elapsed minute 1; the current clock is 0, so it has not expired yet" (probe p12a).
  - (d) The system prompt (protocol.ts:240-243) routes "update_clock for time". update_clock's description (toolUpdateClock.ts:11) says "Update the in-game clock", but it only sets a label. Probe p21: update_clock "Day 2, dawn" leaves elapsed at 0, the wand stays at 0 charges, and a stable PC stays at 0 HP.
  - (e) The prompt routes dawn to reset_usage (protocol.ts:306-308). reset_usage's own description excludes pack-bound items. Probe p22: the wand stays at 0.
  - (f) advance_time is the only truthful driver. The system prompt gives no guidance to use it. It is gated requiresExplicitAction (toolRest.ts:59-63) and listed under the "Inventory and Equipment Guard": "Call them ONLY when the player is explicitly doing something - receiving, purchasing, dropping, using, or losing an item". The auditor rule mirrors this (turnAuditor.ts:269-282).
  - The limit is disclosed only in docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md:143-146 ("minute = 10 rounds ... in combat is not auto-converted"). It is absent from the start_effect, begin_turn and close_combat_instance inventory exclusions, from the model-facing descriptions, and from the candidate record's explicit limits.
- Reachability: live. It affects every minute, hour or day effect started in combat (Bless, Bane, Haste, Hold Person, Shield of Faith, Spiritual Weapon...), every dawn-recharging pack-bound item, and every stable recovery.
- Consequence:
  - Canonical state and the DM context show effects as active past their printed duration. This causes wrong bonuses and spurious concentration saves.
  - On the instructed path, dawn recharges and 1d4-hour recovery never fire.
  - The engine tells the DM, falsely, that an effect "has not expired yet".
- Severity reasoning: a truthful path exists. Probe p12b: advance_time 1 at round 12 expires Bless with end_reason expired. A "ruled" ending also works but misattributes the cause. So this is NON-BLOCKER. The reconciler may weigh the o9bd.16 L3-F2/F3 precedent, where in-band presentation contradicting the live contract was a BLOCKER.
- Siblings:
  - Round-unit spells are refused outside combat (activeEffects.ts:2508-2512). This is the fail-closed mirror.
  - Item timers, stable recovery and short-rest windows share the same elapsed clock (p21).
  - Round timers anchored to the instance expire correctly (deadlineRound; close).
- Suggested closure, either:
  - convert world-time timers anchored in an active combat to the round clock, or advance elapsed time by rounds x 6 s at combat boundaries; or
  - declare the limit in-band: the system prompt names advance_time as the sole way to pass time, update_clock is label-only, and rounds do not advance time; carve time passage out of the explicit-action guard; add the start_effect, begin_turn, close_combat_instance and update_clock exclusions; and admit "expired" once the declared elapsed rounds reach the duration.

  Evidence: an invariant test that a 1-minute concentration effect cast in round r is not live at round r+10 (or that the in-band path ends it as "expired"), plus a prompt-contract test.
- Recurrence alias: related to the o9bd.16 L3 class (model-facing contract versus live behaviour). No registry row.

A2-F3 | NON-BLOCKER | Restored or forked checkpoint copies keep the campaign id that custody uses as writer identity. After a crash, resuming a restored copy is classified "already-held", skips the stale-copy guard, and its release silently rewrites the registry head to an older lineage.
- Invariant and authority:
  - ADR 0012 (0012-character-continuity-and-custody.md:156-158): "no path silently merges or rewrites a character's timeline".
  - characterCustody.ts:1-31: "owned, at any moment, by exactly one writer".
  - The registry row engine-capability-ownership lists "guarded resume" as in force.
  - §5.9 conditions 6 and 8.
- Evidence:
  - characterCustody.ts:536-552: classifyResumeConflict returns already-held on a matching campaignId/characterId, before the head comparison at :554-568.
  - syncBack (:356-367) accepts any DB whose campaign id matches.
  - Checkpoint restore and fork copy meta campaign_id verbatim (serialize.ts, store.ts; CLI checkpoints.ts).
  - CLI play.ts:62-66 runs activateCampaignCustody on any DB, including ESHYRA_DB_PATH. playClose.ts:36-58 releases custody on /quit.
  - Probe p16-custody-restore.ts:
    - register;
    - session 1 release -> rev2, checkpoint K1;
    - session 2 release -> rev3 (xp-900);
    - session 3 acquire, then crash;
    - restore K1;
    - classify the restored copy -> already-held -> acquire -> release commits rev4 (xp-150);
    - the head is now the older lineage.
  - Contrast in the same probe: with idle custody the same restored copy is classified stale-copy.
- Reachability: a live CLI path, but it needs a crash (custody not released), an explicit checkpoint restore or fork, and play of the restored DB. Concurrent play of the original and a copy also triggers it.
- Consequence: the registry head, which every future checkout or catch-up uses, regresses to an older lineage without the stale-copy prompt. The original campaign's next resume then gets stale-copy, whose primary resolution ("catch up to head") would discard its newer progress. Older revisions remain in history, so the state is recoverable rather than destroyed.
- Siblings:
  - Same-slot idempotent re-checkout compares the campaign copy with the head: guarded.
  - catchUp refuses held-elsewhere.
  - Dispute replay is within one DB: no custody effect.
  - Checkpoint fork behaves the same as restore.
- Suggested closure: bind custody to a per-database lineage identity that is minted at creation and re-minted on restore or fork. Alternatively, compare the sheet or sourceRevision with the registry head even when already-held. Evidence: a test where crash, restore and resume yields stale-copy or a refusal, while the original's resume is unaffected.
- Recurrence alias: related to the o9bd.16 L5-F1 class (restore paths losing runtime-significant identity). This is a new manifestation.

A2-F4 | NON-BLOCKER (low) | Level-up HP applies a per-level minimum of 1 and attributes it to "the SRD floor"; SRD 5.1 has no such floor
- Invariant and authority:
  - SRD p.56: "Roll that Hit Die, add your Constitution modifier to the roll, and add the total to your hit point maximum. Alternatively, you can use the fixed value...". Also p.81.
  - A search of the SRD for "minimum of 1" finds only p.50 (Dark One's Blessing), p.86 (suffocation) and p.251 (Winged Boots).
- Evidence: levelUpEngine.ts:1754-1765 (comment "with the SRD floor of at least 1 HP per level"; Math.max(1, average + con)), :1791 (rolled), :1541 (Con-ASI path).
- Reachability: live level-up, but only when the Con modifier is negative and the roll (or average) plus Con is <= 0. Example: a Con 8 wizard rolling 1 on a d6.
- Consequence: HP maximum is 1 higher per affected level than the SRD gives, and the engine documentation falsely attributes the floor to the SRD.
- Siblings: the other Math.max(1, sites are SRD-sourced: calc.ts:257 (food), calc.ts:300 (suffocation), srdClassSpellcasting.ts:146 and requiredChoices.ts:574 (prepared minimum), rest.ts:717 (long-rest hit dice). Query: grep -rn "Math.max(1," packages/core/src.
- Suggested closure: remove the floor or make it an explicit house rule, and correct the comment. Test: Con -1 with a rolled 1 gives +0.
- Recurrence alias: none.

NO-REQUIREMENT OBSERVATIONS:
- Initiative order is not persisted. This is disclosed: "Initiative order ... stay your rulings".
- Most class-feature economies are declared by the DM on the first spend_usage, which its description discloses. Rage, Ki and Sorcery Points derive from the class tables (Rage at level 1 verified).
- resolve_damage resistances and immunities are DM-declared. update_combatant applies hpDelta as given, with no double application (probe p18).
- Damage at 0 HP counts temp-HP-absorbed damage toward failures and instant death. This is an explicit, commented ruling on an SRD p.98 ambiguity.
- The long-rest 24 h refusal does not name the participant. UX only.
- Cape of the Mountebank's cast-dimension-door has no typed activation, so use_item reports the turn resource as not spent and the DM spends it.

LIMITS:
- Scripted model only. No live DM or LLM-auditor run; the auditor's gating of advance_time is inferred from its prompt text.
- Fault injection covered 17 tools. Item, rest, start_effect, start_encounter and currency tools were not fault-injected.
- The checkpoint round trip covered one rich state. Grants, summons, retained checks, rest events and items were not round-tripped.
- Summons, bonded summons and item grant/credit flows were not re-traced (o9bd.16 L4/L5 scope).
- Migrations: FK-action and rebuild review plus runner semantics only. No upgrade of a real older-build DB.
- SRD fidelity was checked only for the records the traced flows consume.
- Discovery, packet, source fidelity and provenance belong to other lanes. Multiclass is excluded (ADR 0018).
